description: Get a repository into a working state safely — for a collaborator onboarding, a fresh clone on a new machine, or catching up an existing clone at the start of a session ("sync me up," "pull the latest," "get this running"). Detects the actual stack from lockfiles, manifests, and the repo's own documented setup commands instead of assuming Python or Node by default, then runs the real install/sync steps. Use also when a startup or session hook is firing more than once and needs diagnosing (not just re-registered), when the user asks to commit, push, or clean up git history and the request could touch shared history or discard work, or when deciding whether a lifecycle hook is genuinely needed for behavior that must happen before the first prompt. Never stashes, merges, rebases, force-pushes, or discards uncommitted work silently to make a setup step "look" successful — a dirty working tree always stops for a decision instead.
